sentences.text: Kamlawati vs Union Of India And 2 Others on 16 April, 2024

Author: Manoj Kumar Gupta
Bench: Manoj Kumar Gupta
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:66764-Db
Court No. - 21
Case :- Writ - C No. - 10299 of 2024
Petitioner :- Kamlawati
Respondent :- Union Of India And 2 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Harish Chandra

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- A.S.G.I.,C.S.C.
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra,J.
1.

The prayer made in the instant petition is for a direction to the respondents to take proper measurement of Arazi no.189 area 0.1720 hectare so that only the area acquired i.e., 0.1570 hectare of plot no.189 remains in the possession of NHAI and the remaining land is handed over to the petitioner and to decide her representations made in this behalf.
2.

The admitted case of the petitioner is that she was awarded compensation for an area measuring 0.1570 hectare of Arazi no.189 in pursuance of the land acquisition proceedings under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956.
The respondents have, in the process, taken over an excess area of land measuring 0.015 hectare.

It is in respect of the said area that the reliefs quoted Kamlawati vs Union Of India And 2 Others on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29775838/
1 above are being claimed.

entities.text: Kamlawati vs Union Of India And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Shri Rajiv Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel appearing for the State-respondents is in receipt of written instructions from ADM, Land Acquisition/Competent Authority, according to which, the petitioner had been paid compensation for 0.1576 hectare.
The report of spot inspection reveals that the respondents have constructed road over an area affecting 0.1716 hectare of Plot no.189.

It is stated that the respondents would initiate proceedings under Section 3A/3D of National Highways Act in respect of excess area taken over by them (0.0140 hectare) and after award is declared in respect of the said area, they would pay compensation to the petitioner.

4. Once it is admitted that the respondents have already utilized some extra land for construction of road, we fail to understand how the respondent would now proceed to notify the said area under Section 3A/3D.
In our opinion, the said exercise should have been done before taking possession of the excess area.

5. Be that as it may, since the respondents admit that they have already taken over possession of excess area, we are of the opinion that the petitioner should be paid compensation for the said area at the same rate at which she was awarded compensation for the land which was covered by the notifications issued under the National Highways Act, 1956.
The said exercise can be held by the District Level Committee in terms of Government Order dated 12.05.2016 whereunder it has power to deal with such kind of cases.

6. Shri Rajiv Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel also fairly states that the matter relating to the calculation of the amount to be paid as compensation to the petitioner be referred to the said committee.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioner has also shown willingness to approach the said committee.

8. The writ petition is accordingly, disposed of with direction to District Level Committee to calculate compensation at par with the rate applied for determining compensation for the acquired land i.e., area measuring 0.1576 hectare within a period of eight weeks from the date of communication of the instant order.
The said amount shall thereafter be paid to the petitioner within next two weeks.
(Kshitij Shailendra, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) Order Date :- 16.4.2024
Ankit.
